defect: A doer burns its whole allowance against an oracle that never ran
evidence: ADR-0057's guard catches a suite that shrank and does not fire when the check cannot execute at all; the doer sees red and has no way to tell a broken oracle from broken code. Found by defect 23, not fixed — the runtime is frozen for this round

defect: A round's first request fails because /health is 200 before any model is loaded
evidence: the first iteration came back 500 "Context size has been exceeded" six seconds in; the router logs show it was still spawning the child instance. n_ctx_slot is 8192 for both models and the message named the wrong cause

defect: No sampling seed is set so no round is reproducible
evidence: the same model on the same slice reached green 6/10 to 10/10; Q7's paired design controls the starting state and not the sampling, so it cannot separate a model's weakness from a bad draw. Budget carries no seed field, so fixing it is a runtime change

defect: A wasted step records the harness's own words and not the model's
evidence: 578 steps across three cells read 'no tool call; nothing happened' and turn.content was discarded, so nothing in the data could say whether the model was planning, refusing, or writing a diff in prose; D6's prompt change had to be designed without it

defect: The model is reloaded on every iteration because the loops alternate
evidence: 122 reloads in one round; the router holds one model under --models-max 1 so each switch reads ~6 GB off disk and pushes it to VRAM, measured at 466% of one core for the two minutes after a spawn. BENCH_BLOCK now groups iterations, default 1 because alternating protects against a 20-point swing between a cell's halves

defect: The model is resident twice: 7.34 GB of private RAM alongside 7.87 GB of VRAM
evidence: PARKED 2026-10-16: found, not explained, and not being chased. Private (7.34 GB) above WorkingSet (6.14 GB) ruled out the memory-mapped file, which was the first hypothesis, and measuring -lm auto against -lm mmap ruled it out again (7.21 GB against 7.17 GB). Remaining candidates: the loader keeping a host copy, and CUDA pinned staging. Parked because one model is resident at a time on this machine and 31.8 GB of RAM absorbs one extra copy; it becomes real again the day two models are loaded together or the host runs something large beside the server

defect: A round runs with 149 MiB of VRAM to spare and the desktop competes for it
evidence: 7870 of 8192 MiB used on an RTX 3070 with the model loaded; 0.3 GB had already spilled to shared memory, which is system RAM over PCIe. Browsers, Steam, Zoom and VS Code were all holding GPU memory at the same time

defect: The GPU driver version is not recorded anywhere
evidence: cells 1-6 ran on 610.88 and an update to 617.42 was offered mid-round; nothing in round.txt would have said which stack a number came from. Same class as defect 26 — an environment variable that moves the result and that nobody wrote down

defect: The oracle preflight disagreed with the parser it was protecting
evidence: the preflight matched a regular expression shaped like cargo and pytest output; vitest prints 'Tests  26 failed (26)' with no duration, so an all-red scaffolded suite — the correct starting state — read as an oracle that could not run. It now asks the runtime's own counter through bench/src/bin/count.rs

defect: The FINAL row carried a per-language result line that no reader could compare
evidence: 'test result: ok. 26 passed; 0 failed' in Rust, '26 passed' in Python, nothing matchable in TypeScript. Now counted by the same parser and written as ran/passed; analyse.py reads both forms because the earlier rows are committed

defect: Rewriting a file with identical bytes cleared the repeat history
evidence: ADR-0050 §4 resets the detector when an artefact changes, and every successful write counted as a change. A model writing the same bytes forever therefore reset the detector on every step and was never warned; observed as six identical writes with limits.repeats set to 1. Fixed: the bytes are compared first, and the model is told when nothing changed

defect: `ownership` is keyed by file class and was read as keyed by role
evidence: the first draft of the config-to-runtime conversion looked up config.ownership[role] expecting classes; the map is class to roles. Caught by the configuration validator before any run, which named both halves of the mistake

defect: The llama.cpp request was built twice and only one copy was tested
evidence: extracting `body` as a testable seam left `chat` building its own copy, so four wire tests asserted a function production never called. They had already drifted: the temperature reached the shipping copy and not the tested one. Found by a test that failed for the right reason

defect: Every round and probe ran at llama.cpp's default temperature of 0.80
evidence: nobody set it and nobody recorded it, the same class as defect 26. High for code — prose survives a word chosen second-best and code does not compile. The probe watched one model score 5 of 10 then 10 of 10 under identical flags and that was read as the model's variance when it may have been the sampler's

defect: The llama.cpp build is not recorded in any round
evidence: the runtime decides what a model does with a prompt and it updates itself — `llama update` has no help page and performs the update when asked for one, which is how this build went from 11574 to 11671 mid-session. Same class as defect 31, and round.txt now carries it beside the commit, the seed and the driver

defect: `think: false` asked the server not to parse thinking rather than not to think
evidence: corifeu-llamacpp sent reasoning_format=none, whose own help says it 'leaves thoughts unparsed in message.content'. The model therefore thought anyway and wrote the thinking into the answer, spending num_predict and putting prose where a tool call belongs. Measured on one prompt: 175 tokens asking for 'none' against 2 asking the template not to think. A strong candidate for round five's 32% of steps cut off before calling a tool

defect: The probe inverted its own thinking switch and hid where the tokens went
evidence: `enable_thinking: not args.think` meant thinking was on whenever --think was absent, so three samples spent 6144 tokens and scored 0; and ask.py saved only `content`, so a reply with an empty content and a spent budget left nothing on disk saying why. reasoning_content is written out now

defect: The model card was read after the measurements rather than before
evidence: it asks for at least 128K of context to preserve thinking, which an 8 GB card cannot give, so 'this model does not converge when thinking' was really 'thinking is unusable on this hardware'. It also recommends temperature 0.6 with top_k 20 and min_p 0.0 for precise coding, against the 0.1-0.2 and llama.cpp defaults used here, and an output length of 32768 against the 6144 used

defect: The VRAM projection for 64k left out the MTP draft context
evidence: 64k with a q8 cache was projected to fit and did not: the weights alone are 5855 MiB and the load log announces a second allocation, `common_speculative_init_result: creating MTP draft context against the target model`, which the arithmetic never counted. 48k is the measured ceiling, 321 MiB free, 96-112 tok/s

defect: The probe accepted a host with no port and then crashed reporting it
evidence: --host 192.168.32.1 built http://192.168.32.1/v1/chat/completions, which is port 80, and the refused connection read as a dead server; the handler then wrote error.txt into an --out directory it had never created, so the only trace was a FileNotFoundError about the error file. ask.py now rejects a host without a port and creates --out

defect: A round recorded its seed and not its temperature
evidence: eight passes at one seed base — four greedy, four sampled, two without speculative decoding — produced round.txt headers identical apart from the timestamp, so no stored record could tell them apart. The round itself showed why it matters: at temperature 0 the ten different seeds inside a pass gave byte-identical output, so 'two runs at one seed agreed' means nothing without the temperature beside it. bench/run.sh now writes temp, server and spec lines, read from /props and /slots by bench/server.py

defect: The server reports speculative decoding as off on the endpoint most likely to be asked
evidence: /props returns `speculative.types: none` in default_generation_settings while MTP is loaded and drafting — the truth is on /slots, as `speculative: true` and `params.speculative.types: none,draft-mtp`. Recording the configuration from /props would have stamped 'no MTP' on a round that ran with it, and the 2.3x wall-clock difference between the E/F and G/H passes is what proves MTP was active

defect: An agent CLI reports almost no input tokens because its context arrives as cache reads
evidence: two claude -p calls reported usage.input_tokens = 2 while cache_read_input_tokens was 8857 and 11639 and total_cost_usd was 0.1086 and 0.0839. Reading tokens per role from input_tokens alone would show the expensive planner consuming two tokens against the local coder's thousands, and ADR-0031's savings figure would claim a discount near 100% — wrong in the direction that flatters the project. The run record has to carry total_cost_usd per role, with the cache fields beside the input count

defect: The flag ADR-0007 names for ignoring ambient context also removes the credential
evidence: claude -p --bare returns is_error true with result 'Not logged in · Please run /login'. ADR-0007 lists --bare as how Claude Code ignores user and global context, which ADR-0014 requires of an adapter; --setting-sources is narrower but takes user,project,local and rejects an empty value, so full neutralisation is unavailable on 2.1.302. The adapter uses --restricted --strict-mcp-config and the user's own settings come along

defect: An agent CLI acts on the prompt instead of proposing the call
evidence: asked to 'Call write_file with path src/a.ts', claude -p used its own Write tool, failed on permissions and spent 0.048 USD reporting that — it did the task rather than proposing it. Rephrased as 'You are proposing one action for another program to carry out. Do not act', it answered with the JSON call. Corifeu's loop executes tools, so the adapter's system message has to say so. Separately, without stdin redirected the CLI prints a three-second stdin warning before the JSON, so the adapter reads from the first brace

defect: Corifeu put nondeterministic text into its own prompts
evidence: a check's output goes into the next step's prompt and corifeu-exec returned it raw. Two runs of one unchanged crate differ twice over: cargo prints 'Finished ... in 0.22s' against 'in 0.13s', and runs tests on a thread per core so the completion order changes. Under greedy decoding either is enough to flip a token and every token after it, which is why a seeded round replays at one step per slice and not at twelve — round seven's 159 of 160 was measured on one-step slices and does not generalise. Fixed by corifeu_exec::steady, which replaces a duration with Xs, and by the Rust tasks' oracles taking --test-threads=1

defect: A failing test puts the OS thread it ran on into the next prompt
evidence: the Rust harness prints `thread 'slice1_tokens::parens' (186718) panicked`, and that number is different every run. Round nine found it by dumping the prompts of two passes and diffing them; the step trace keeps only the first line of a result, so it was invisible. Beside it, the workspace's absolute path carries the round's own directory name, so two rounds differ by construction. corifeu_exec::settled replaces the thread id with T and the working directory with a dot, which also stops asking the model about a path it cannot leave

defect: A round that is committed to while it runs is not one configuration
evidence: two replay passes recorded commit 8eaa719 and 00ebf5e because bench/run.sh rebuilds at the start of each round and the repo was being committed to between them. The comparison measured two binaries and was reported as a replay result before round.txt's commit line showed it. run.sh should refuse to start on a dirty tree, or record the build rather than HEAD
